body: This template is intentionally vault-local rather than a shipped domain template. It describes how future agents should maintain AWG knowledge while preserving the project constraints: deterministic local files, append-only canonical logs, minimal dependencies, and domain-agnostic behavior.

fields.approval_rules: Agents may update working knowledge but must not self-approve templates, policy, client-visible output, high-risk scope changes, pricing, ownership, or release decisions. Preserve human_approved and review_state unless the human explicitly changes them.
fields.backup_rules: Keep the project-local .awg vault in version control with append-only source logs. Before high-stakes migrations or exports, verify git status and prefer deterministic build/doctor checks over manual backup edits.
fields.capture_policy: Capture future-affecting decisions, requirements, risks, blockers, evidence, source-of-truth boundaries, workflow friction, and accepted operating rules. Prefer updating canonical nodes over creating duplicates.
fields.coordination_rules: Claim non-trivial shared work before acting, check for existing claims on claimed targets, release or hand off claims before stopping, and treat coordination as collision avoidance rather than a hard lock.
fields.cross_vault_rules: Write only to the explicit current vault. For related vaults, use topology and summary-level context; switch cwd before writing there or leave a handoff task instead of mutating another vault indirectly.
fields.evidence_rules: Treat implementation, verification, approvals, and stale external claims as unproven until supported by command, test, file, manual, system, or redacted evidence. Mark evidence-required work incomplete until proof is attached or explicitly carried forward.
fields.export_rules: Exports and handoffs should be minimal, redacted, and scoped to the recipient. Include node IDs, summaries, status, evidence pointers, and open risks without leaking private content or unrelated vault context.
fields.lens_rules: Start with built-in resume, task, handoff, and current-view lenses. Create or revise configurable lenses only for repeated context shapes, keep them compact and query-backed, and leave new lenses needs_review unless human-approved.
fields.maintenance_rules: Search before adding knowledge, update stale canonical nodes, reconcile duplicates or contradictions explicitly, close resolved tasks and risks with evidence, and leave intentional carry-forward items visible rather than orphaned.
fields.non_capture_policy: Do not store raw transcripts, scratch reasoning, secrets, credentials, private excerpts, or facts whose source of truth is code, docs, tests, tickets, or external systems unless a durable consequence needs an AWG summary.
fields.queue_rules: Use queue priority as context, not permission to override the user. Autonomous queue work must be narrow, reversible, evidenced, and within current vault scope; human-review items stay review-only until approved.
fields.retention_rules: Retain durable project memory, decisions, evidence, risks, and current operating policy. Archive or supersede stale material instead of deleting it, and avoid retaining low-value chat residue or sensitive source material.
fields.sensitivity_rules: Redact credentials, tokens, private client data, financial details, personal data, and sensitive excerpts. Store only minimal summaries needed for future work, and prefer source references over copied sensitive content.
fields.view_rules: Keep human views concise, current, and action-oriented. Surface blockers, risks, stale decisions, active tasks, and verification state; avoid dumping raw graph detail when a summary or node link is clearer.

body:
## Problem
When AWG gains new capabilities, agents may keep using older workflows unless the human explains the change. That creates adoption drag and makes new features less valuable.

## Desired Behavior
Each release should expose deterministic, local release notes for agents. On startup, handoff, resume, or instruction install/upgrade, agents should be able to see what changed, what new commands are available, and whether the current vault has recommended migrations or optional adoption steps.

## V1.9.1 Scope
Add a local release-notes surface and agent instruction pointer. Prefer a concise file or compiled artifact plus CLI read path such as awg release notes, awg release current, or awg changelog. Generated AGENTS guidance should point agents to it without bloating AGENTS.md with every release. Release notes should include date/version, highlights, agent actions, migration/adoption suggestions, and links to docs/nodes where useful.

## Deferred Packaging Scope
A true awg update command belongs later, once distribution through npm or another stable install channel exists. Until then, focus on local awareness and upgrade notes rather than package self-update.

## Constraints
Keep this local-first and deterministic. Do not add hosted sync, network checks, daemon behavior, or auto-mutation of vaults without explicit commands. Agents may suggest adoption or run safe diagnostics, but should not silently rewrite project knowledge just because a feature exists.

body:
# V1.8 Subagent Review Synthesis

Three independent review agents inspected the V1.8 AWG planning cluster for implementation readiness.

## Consensus

The architecture is correct: explicit topology plus read-mostly federation is the right foundation. The original cluster was discoverable through `awg lens task`, but it was too high-level for a fresh implementation agent to safely build without making product/API decisions.

## Gaps Found

- Vault identity was called stable, but current registry IDs are path-derived and would break when projects move.
- Relationship storage location and JSON shape were not final enough.
- Relationship vocabulary drifted between `provides_schema_for`, `consumes_data_from`, `provides_contract_for`, `consumes_contract_from`, `owns`, and `owned_by`.
- Cross-vault refs had no concrete node field shape.
- Cross-vault handoff/update obligations had no deterministic representation.
- CLI selector rules, JSON outputs, error codes, duplicate behavior, and unlink/archive behavior were not specified.
- Federation output and relevance rules were too vague to test.
- Privacy/visibility behavior needed a conservative V1 contract.
- The current task lens surfaces node summaries but not enough body detail for implementation, so V1.8 should add or document a node-detail retrieval path.
- Test coverage needed explicit failure-mode cases.

## Resulting Action

The review findings were incorporated into implementation-grade AWG spec nodes covering topology contracts, CLI/JSON behavior, retrieval/preflight/handoff behavior, and tests. These nodes should be treated as required implementation inputs before coding V1.8.
summary: Three subagent reviews found V1.8 architecturally sound but not implementation-ready until identity, schema, CLI, retrieval, preflight, and test contracts were made explicit.

body: This template is intentionally vault-local rather than a shipped domain template. It describes how future agents should maintain AWG knowledge while preserving the project constraints: deterministic local files, append-only canonical logs, minimal dependencies, and domain-agnostic behavior.

fields.agent_rules: Start with awg handoff, awg run start, awg template status --goal, awg search, and awg lens task. Use summaries for scanning, body for durable detail, fields for structured facts, safe blocks for presentation, freshness for currentness, anchors for references, and evidence for completed work. Do not edit .awg/compiled as source or add network/daemon/AI/vector/plugin scope without explicit approval.
fields.approval_rules: Agents may update working knowledge but must not self-approve templates, policy, client-visible output, high-risk scope changes, pricing, ownership, or release decisions. Preserve human_approved and review_state unless the human explicitly changes them.
fields.backup_rules: Keep the project-local .awg vault in version control with append-only source logs. Before high-stakes migrations or exports, verify git status and prefer deterministic build/doctor checks over manual backup edits.
fields.capture_policy: Capture future-affecting decisions, requirements, risks, blockers, evidence, source-of-truth boundaries, workflow friction, and accepted operating rules. Prefer updating canonical nodes over creating duplicates.
fields.change_rationale: Reset approval metadata because historical template approval was agent-authored, not durable human approval evidence.
fields.coordination_rules: Claim non-trivial shared work before acting, check for existing claims on claimed targets, release or hand off claims before stopping, and treat coordination as collision avoidance rather than a hard lock.
fields.cross_vault_rules: Write only to the explicit current vault. For related vaults, use topology and summary-level context; switch cwd before writing there or leave a handoff task instead of mutating another vault indirectly.
fields.evidence_rules: Treat implementation, verification, approvals, and stale external claims as unproven until supported by command, test, file, manual, system, or redacted evidence. Mark evidence-required work incomplete until proof is attached or explicitly carried forward.
fields.export_rules: Exports and handoffs should be minimal, redacted, and scoped to the recipient. Include node IDs, summaries, status, evidence pointers, and open risks without leaking private content or unrelated vault context.
fields.freshness_rules: Review and update related current nodes whenever CLI behavior, compiler output, diagnostics, viewer surfaces, generated instructions, docs, or agent workflow expectations change.
fields.lens_rules: Start with built-in resume, task, handoff, and current-view lenses. Create or revise configurable lenses only for repeated context shapes, keep them compact and query-backed, and leave new lenses needs_review unless human-approved.
fields.maintenance_rules: Search before adding knowledge, update stale canonical nodes, reconcile duplicates or contradictions explicitly, close resolved tasks and risks with evidence, and leave intentional carry-forward items visible rather than orphaned.
fields.migration_notes: Future agents should keep this template needs_review until Timothy explicitly approves it.
fields.non_capture_policy: Do not store raw transcripts, scratch reasoning, secrets, credentials, private excerpts, or facts whose source of truth is code, docs, tests, tickets, or external systems unless a durable consequence needs an AWG summary.
fields.purpose: Guide agents maintaining AWG as a local-first, deterministic, append-only, domain-agnostic shared agent brain with a human presentation layer.
fields.queue_rules: Use queue priority as context, not permission to override the user. Autonomous queue work must be narrow, reversible, evidenced, and within current vault scope; human-review items stay review-only until approved.
fields.retention_rules: Retain durable project memory, decisions, evidence, risks, and current operating policy. Archive or supersede stale material instead of deleting it, and avoid retaining low-value chat residue or sensitive source material.
fields.sensitivity_rules: Redact credentials, tokens, private client data, financial details, personal data, and sensitive excerpts. Store only minimal summaries needed for future work, and prefer source references over copied sensitive content.
fields.view_rules: Keep human views concise, current, and action-oriented. Surface blockers, risks, stale decisions, active tasks, and verification state; avoid dumping raw graph detail when a summary or node link is clearer.

body:
## Scope
Implement lifecycle closeout and attention hygiene for long-lived AWG vaults.

## Core idea
Separate durable lifecycle status from derived attention state. A node can remain active or needs_review without being treated as current focus forever. Current focus should come from active runs, coordination claims, goal relevance, recent touches, urgent diagnostics, and explicit review dates rather than status alone.

## Required foundation
- Derive graph.attention_index and .awg/compiled/indexes/attention.json.
- Add closeout candidates for old open work likely completed, resolved, superseded, answered, or intentionally carried forward.
- Add append-only acknowledgements for intentionally carried-forward open items with reason and review date.
- Add bounded closeout/sweep CLI surfaces without bulk automatic mutation.
- Integrate attention into work queues, current view, handoff, resume/task lenses, run finish preflight, doctor, inbox, and optionally the viewer.

## Source spec
See docs/spec/awg-lifecycle-closeout-attention.md for the full implementation contract, JSON shapes, command contracts, tests, verification, and non-goals.
